div.head: VI As Prolog
div.ab: Hoc est constitutum (consultum) quod episcopi et prepositi, qui Londoniensi curie pertinent, edixerunt et iureiurando confirmauerunt in suo friðgildo, comites et uillani, adiectione iudiciorum que apud Greateleiam et Exoniam instituta sunt et item apud Þunresfeldam.

Ðis is seo gerǽdnes, þe þa biscopas ⁊ þa gerefan, þe to Lundenbyrig hyrað, gecweden habbað ⁊ mid weddum gefæstnod on urum friðgegyldum, ægðer ge eorlisce ge ceorlisce, to ecan þam domum, þe æt Gréatanléa ⁊ æt Exanceastre gesette wæron ⁊ æt Þunresfelda.

Ðis is seo gerǽdnes þe þa biscopas ⁊ þa gerefan þe to Lundenbyrig hyrað gecweden habbað, ⁊ mid weddum gefæstnod on urum friðgegyldum, ægðer ge eorlisce ge ceorlisce, to ecan þam domum þe æt Gréatanléa ⁊ æt Exanceastre gesette wæron, ⁊ æt Þunresfelda.

These are the ordinances which have been agreed upon and confirmed with solemn declarations in our association, by the bishops and reeves who belong to London—both by nobles and commoners—as a supplement to the decrees which were promulgated at Grately, and Exeter, and at Thundersfield(?).

This is the ordinance which the bishops and the reeves who belong to London have agreed to and confirmed with pledges in our peace-guild, both nobles and ceorls, addition to the statutes which were established at Grately and at Exeter and at Thunderfield.

Prolog. Dies ist der Beschluss, welchen die Bischöfe und die Vögte, welche zu London[s Gerichtsbezirk durch ihre Hintersassen] zugehören, verkündet und durch rechtsförmliche Verpflichtungen bekräftigt haben in unserer Friedensgilde [oder unseren F.-Verträgen], sowohl vornehme wie gemeinfreie, zur Ergänzung für die Gesetze, welche zu Greatley und zu Exeter und zu Thundersfield festgesetzt worden waren.

Prologue. This is the ordinance which the bishops and the reeves who belong to London['s jurisdiction through their tenants] have proclaimed and confirmed by formal pledges in our peace-guild [or our peace-agreements], both noble and common freemen, as a supplement to the laws which had been established at Greatley and at Exeter and at Thundersfield.
div.note: ‘eft’ was read here by Quadr. (Liebermann). Liebermann compares II, V, IV As.
A rhyming formula: ge eorlisce ge ceorlisce. see p. 410, n. 2.

Probably Thunderfield, Surrey, which has the proper early form in King Alfred's will and in Birch, No. 820. An O.E. fragment of laws issued there exists, and a longer Latin text. This code is cited as IV Athelstan.
